source.authors: Xie H, Yuan H, Wang Y, Tang X, Yang M, Zheng L, Li Z
source.title: Compound Eye Structure and Phototactic Dimorphism in the Yunnan Pine Shoot Beetle, Tomicus yunnanensis (Coleoptera: Scolytinae)

method: scanning electron microscopy; facets counted on micrographs (counting procedure not described)
conditions: adults collected alive within pine stems or shoots in January-February (year not printed), JiuLong Shan Forestry Station, central Yunnan, China; SEM on detached heads of 10 males and 15 females (Section 2.2) but Table 1 lists n = 14 males and n = 16 females for facet number (unexplained); mean ± dispersion measure (SD or SE) not stated; the same sentence gives both sexes (males 240.00 ± 3.51, females 247.38 ± 3.18); no test between sexes reported for facet number in Results (Methods name unpaired t-tests; the Discussion says significant sexual dimorphism in facet number is absent in bark beetles); the preceding sentence states that left and right eyes differ in facet number and surface-area distribution (which eye was counted is not stated); sexes kept as separate records
where: Results, Section 3.1 Gross External Morphology of the Eye
quote: Males possessed an average of 240.00 ± 3.51 facets per eye, while females had 247.38 ± 3.18 facets per eye.
note: new trait: ommatidia_count (key already in use on main). Page prints no licence sentence (metadata CC BY 3.0); one Crossref single-DOI lookup gave CC BY 4.0, content-version vor. Order as printed in the paper's title; the title gives the subfamily Scolytinae only, so family is left blank. Name filed as printed. The same paper's phototaxis result is already on main (desk-d227, behaviour_vision).

source.authors: Xie H, Yuan H, Wang Y, Tang X, Yang M, Zheng L, Li Z
source.title: Compound Eye Structure and Phototactic Dimorphism in the Yunnan Pine Shoot Beetle, Tomicus yunnanensis (Coleoptera: Scolytinae)

eye: central rhabdomere (R7 and R8) of the ommatidium
method: light and transmission electron microscopy of sectioned eyes (Section 3.2.3)
conditions: eyes of both sexes examined by LM and TEM with at least three replicates per sex/treatment group (Section 2); sex of the measured eyes not stated; Table 1 gives n = 6 (peripheral) and n = 17 (central) rhabdomeres; dispersion measure not stated; one sentence gives both lengths (peripheral 11.9 ± 0.5, central 43.5 ± 1.6) and calls the central rhabdomere 'significantly longer' without a test statistic in the sentence; collected January-February (year not printed), JiuLong Shan Forestry Station, Yunnan, China
where: Results, Section 3.2.3 Retinular Cells and Rhabdom
quote: Within this structure, the rhabdomeres of the six peripheral cells (R1–R6), measuring 11.9 ± 0.5 µm in length, encircle the central rhabdomere formed by R7 and R8 (which is significantly longer at 43.5 ± 1.6 µm).
note: Key rhabdom_um already exists. Whole sentence, seen complete in two WebFetch pieces joined with a single space. Page prints no licence sentence (metadata CC BY 3.0); one Crossref single-DOI lookup gave CC BY 4.0, content-version vor. Order as printed in the paper's title; the title gives the subfamily Scolytinae only, so family is left blank. Name filed as printed. The same paper's phototaxis result is already on main (desk-d227, behaviour_vision).

source.title: Compound Eye Structure and Phototactic Dimorphism in the Yunnan Pine Shoot Beetle, Tomicus yunnanensis (Coleoptera: Scolytinae)

method: calculated, not measured directly: interommatidial angle Δφ = A/R, A the maximum facet diameter, R the eye radius estimated geometrically
conditions: sex, number of eyes and individuals for the calculated value not stated; collected January-February (year not printed), JiuLong Shan Forestry Station, Yunnan, China; the Discussion repeats the value
where: Results, Section 3.4 Optical Features of the Compound Eyes
quote: Spatial resolution (interommatidial angle Δφ = A/R) was 3.2°; eye radius R was geometrically estimated (R = (s2/4 + h2)/(2h), s = segment length, h = height).
note: Key interommatidial_deg already exists. Whole sentence seen complete in two WebFetch pieces. Page prints no licence sentence (metadata CC BY 3.0); one Crossref single-DOI lookup gave CC BY 4.0, content-version vor. Order as printed in the paper's title; the title gives the subfamily Scolytinae only, so family is left blank. Name filed as printed. source.authors: Ran H, Li M, Niu Y, Ma A, Yang X
source.title: Anatomy and Ultrastructural Details of the Compound Eyes of the Pear Psyllid, Cacopsylla chinensis (Yang et Li) (Hemiptera: Psyllidae)

method: calculated from corneal-lens diameter and eye radius (87.8 ± 5.2 μm)
conditions: twelve live adults (6 females and 6 males) from a pear orchard in Fanzhuang Town, Zhao County, Hebei, China, collected June 2023, exposed to 1000 lx for 2 h before fixation (Section 2.1); the authors report no sexual dimorphism and combined males and females (per-sex values in Table S1, not seen); number of eyes measured not stated; the sentence states the angle was determined from a corneal-lens diameter of 15.6 ± 0.6 μm, whereas Section 3.1 gives the cornea as 16.9 ± 1.7 μm in diameter and the cone length as 15.6 ± 0.6 μm (an inconsistency in the paper, not resolved here)
quote: The total length of the ommatidium is on average 76.0 ± 3.0 μm, while the average interommatidial angle is 1.9 ± 0.6 deg, determined from the diameter of the corneal lens (15.6 ± 0.6 μm) […]
note: Key interommatidial_deg already exists. Sentence seen complete in two WebFetch pieces; the quote is cut at the end, marked […], for the 40-word limit; the cut text is 'and the eye radius of 87.8 ± 5.2 μm.' Page prints no licence sentence (metadata CC BY 3.0); one Crossref single-DOI lookup gave CC BY 4.0, content-version vor. Family and order as printed in the paper's title. Name filed as printed. The same paper's eye_type and polarization records are already on main (desk-d203).

source.title: Anatomy and Ultrastructural Details of the Compound Eyes of the Pear Psyllid, Cacopsylla chinensis (Yang et Li) (Hemiptera: Psyllidae)

eye: rhabdom of the ommatidium (fused, 8 retinular cells), adult (sexes combined)
conditions: twelve live adults (6 females and 6 males) from a pear orchard in Fanzhuang Town, Zhao County, Hebei, China, collected June 2023, exposed to 1000 lx for 2 h before fixation (Section 2.1); the authors report no sexual dimorphism and combined males and females (per-sex values in Table S1, not seen); 'approximately' as printed; number of rhabdoms measured not stated
where: Results, Section 3.3 Retinula Cells and Rhabdom
quote: Under the crystalline cone lie eight retinular cells forming a centrally fused rhabdom, measuring approximately 57.0 ± 3.6 μm in length.
